findings.title: The immutable slice baseline manifest records post-patch hashes instead of P4-BASE hashes

concrete_reproduction.state: Reconstruct source commit 2960b690bf89232b8a23c5b8823fbe0ca831347f, apply the six P4-BASE r02 predecessor patches in manifest order, and compare the nine existing P4-S1 files with r02/baseline.json and r02/baseline.tar.
concrete_reproduction.wrong_behavior: All nine baseline_sha256 entries in the slice baseline manifest disagree with the reconstructed prepared tree and with the files in baseline.tar. Each recorded value is instead the corresponding post-patch result_sha256 value. For example, internal/runtime/executor/codex_executor.go is ab283a39fe93ae2cc7840ed279fcb61f42c650004a17f72527ee80a9502fd79a in P4-BASE and baseline.tar, while slice baseline.json records dbaeff7db2a90f78d77aa6c4b53d1542ba52967294aa34b408db229db135a1a9, the result hash.
concrete_reproduction.reproduced_result: slice_reverse_archive_hashes_match=true, but slice_reverse_manifest_hashes_match=false; all 9 existing-file manifest comparisons were false. Therefore application-proof.json's prepared_base_hashes_match=true is not reproducible against the immutable slice manifest.

findings.impact: The frozen evidence package is not self-consistent. A consumer using baseline.json cannot verify the archived baseline or a correct reverse application, even though independent full-tree reconstruction and the archive itself are valid.

findings.title: Fragmented custom-tool arguments leak the JSON wrapper in HTTP and WebSocket delta streams

upstream_sequence: response.output_item.added: function_call id fc_1, name patch
response.output_item.done and response.completed for the same call
concrete_reproduction.wrong_behavior: Both transports correctly rename event types and IDs to response.custom_tool_call_input.delta and ctc_1, but each delta is independently passed through unwrapCustomToolInput. Because neither fragment is complete JSON, the emitted delta values remain {"inp and ut":"diff"}; concatenating client-visible custom input deltas yields {"input":"diff"} instead of the declared custom input diff. The done, output_item.done, and completed payloads then report input=diff, so the stream is internally inconsistent.
concrete_reproduction.http_result: TestReviewHTTPFragmentedCustomArguments failed: HTTP custom delta text = "{\"input\":\"diff\"}", want diff.
concrete_reproduction.websocket_result: TestReviewWebSocketFragmentedCustomArguments failed: WebSocket custom delta text = "{\"input\":\"diff\"}", want diff.

findings.impact: Real providers may split function arguments at arbitrary byte boundaries. Clients receive wrapper JSON as custom freeform input during streaming even though terminal events contain the unwrapped input.

findings.title: Chat-Completions-to-Responses custom calls drop every input delta event

concrete_reproduction.request: Responses request declaring custom tool patch.
concrete_reproduction.upstream_state: Two Chat Completions tool-call argument chunks compose {"input":"diff"}, followed by finish_reason=tool_calls.
concrete_reproduction.wrong_behavior: emitPendingFunctionArgs returns immediately for custom items, so the converter emits response.output_item.added, response.custom_tool_call_input.done, and response.output_item.done but no response.custom_tool_call_input.delta event at all, despite receiving upstream argument deltas.
concrete_reproduction.reproduced_result: TestReviewChatStreamEmitsCustomInputDelta failed; captured events were response.created, response.in_progress, custom response.output_item.added, response.custom_tool_call_input.done, and custom response.output_item.done, with no custom input delta.

findings.impact: The custom-tool lifecycle is not complete or consistent across translator paths; streaming consumers cannot observe incremental custom input on this path.

additional_tests.coverage: top-level then additional_tools order, function/custom effective-name collisions, namespaced namespace ending in delimiter, mcp__ byte stability, delimiter-only non-restoration, output-index preservation, and request-local table isolation

other_adversarial_checks.reconnect_and_replay_review: No state-sharing defect found: the declaration table is local to one Execute/ExecuteStream invocation, is created before dial, survives the one send-retry path, and session reqMu serializes requests. No dedicated patch regression covers replay after partial response.
other_adversarial_checks.phase_1_close_1009_behavior: PASS via the frozen executor command, including Execute, ExecuteStream, write/read mapping, and backpressure terminal-error tests

reviewer_notes: The full prepared, forward result, and reverse trees independently reproduce exactly despite the slice baseline manifest hash defect.
The permanent r02 regressions cover only complete JSON argument deltas, so they miss arbitrary provider chunk boundaries.
The WebSocket collision path now returns structured HTTP 400 invalid_request_error/tool_name_collision before dial with zero observed upstream activity.
No product, planning, documentation, patch, baseline, result, proof, or main-tree files were edited. Only this review.json was updated.
review_summary: REJECTED. Patch SHA-256, exact 12-file scope, predecessor hashes, prepared/result/reverse trees, non-slice predecessor stability, forward/reverse application, planned-new deletion, frozen tests, race tests, WebSocket pre-dial collision behavior, covered identity restoration, mcp__ stability, output indices, and Phase 1 close-1009 behavior were independently reproduced. Rejection is required because the immutable baseline manifest contains nine post-patch hashes and falsely claims prepared-base hash agreement, fragmented custom arguments expose wrapper JSON in both HTTP and WebSocket custom delta streams, and the Chat-Completions response translator drops custom input delta events entirely.
